text:
elaine_sales: Quick heads-up — ACME legal/security is asking if we can run their POC inside a sealed site (no outbound). They need a short note for SOW covering: how we deliver bundles, how upgrades/deltas work, license activation story, and rollback. Anyone have the short answers?
sanjay_se: We do support fully offline installs. Two common patterns: 1) jumpbox transfer (customer pulls from our signed bundle hosted externally -> moves into sealed net), 2) physical media (USB/airgap). Key questions: do they require SBOM, firmware signing, or HSM-based attestation?
elaine_sales: They want SBOM + signed artifacts. HSM attestation optional but desirable for SOC2 + their procurement.
jamie_soleng: Tech details: we produce a signed bundle (.tar.gz + detached sig) and a chunk manifest for resumable sideloads. Typical flow: CI builds -> artifact signed with our signing key (or customer's pubkey) -> provide bundle + .sig + manifest. For verification: ```openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz``` or `sha256sum -c bundle.sha256`.
jamie_soleng: For deltas we can ship chunked differential patches. Patch cadence is configurable; recommendation for a POC is weekly deltas for telemetry/fixes, production monthly for security patches, emergency hotfixes as needed. For sealed customers we default to manual activation windows (customer triggers apply) — we do not push automatic updates into sealed nets.
ryan_sec: A few security constraints: we can support HSM-backed signing and key-wrapping for license tokens. Offline cert rotation is a manual CSR flow via jumpbox; rotation frequency can be set (default 90 days). If they require FIPS-validated crypto or hardware attestation, flag that — may add procurement lead time.
elaine_sales: Licensing question from procurement: can license be activated offline?
sanjay_se: Yes — license tokens can be embedded in the bundle or delivered as a signed activation file that the installer consumes. For higher assurance we support HSM-wrapped license blobs that require a local HSM to unwrap. Also support per-tenant license files with expiration.
jamie_soleng: Rollback story: we publish explicit release manifests with stable version hashes; the installer supports rolling back to a pinned version using the manifest. Recommend we offer a canary activation step in the runbook: apply to 1 node, smoke tests, then full. All of this is in the offline runbook we give customers.
deploy-bot: CI artifact v1.12.3 (signed) — size: 2.4GB, chunks: 8, sha256: 3f6a...9c2a, created: 3951112200.
ryan_sec: Operational notes: customers should provision a small jumpbox VM with disk staging and deterministic checksums. Network rules: allow SCP inbound from jumpbox only, no outbound from app cluster. We also recommend time-sync (NTP) for certificate validation.
elaine_sales: Pricing/ops ask: is there a one-time packaging fee?
sanjay_se: Yes, offline packaging + runbook + SOW customization is usually a one-time professional services fee (estimate sent separately). Ongoing: if we provide signed delta builds or HSM key management we may charge an annual maintenance premium.
jamie_soleng: I'll draft the SOW appendix + the offline runbook (install steps, verify commands, rollback, hotfix path) and drop it here by EOD. Example verify snippet I'll include: ```# verify signature
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
# verify manifest
cat manifest.json | jq .chunks | sha256sum -c```
elaine_sales: perfect — once we have the SOW snippet I'll attach to ACME's security questionnaire. thanks :thumbsup:
ryan_sec: One more: if they want automated attestation (device-level), we'll need to provision an attestation endpoint in the private network or accept signed quotes from their HSM provider. That usually takes extra eval time.
elaine_sales: noted — i'll mark attestation optional in the SOW and request their HSM vendor details. thanks everyone.
